comment: Each scenario is one screenshot: a screen of the launcher, the player's games (title IDs, or TITLEID:Name for a game nxnative.json does not have, which IGDB has by its name when the catalogue has a game of that name), whether the setup is done and whether a controller is connected; the game of a sheet or of its settings page, with the page's category (one of nxnative's sections, or cartouche.saves for the cloud saves), or the game being installed with work: installing, or its install that failed, with the report to copy, with work: install-failed, or a new version of Cartouche on offer with work: update, a newer build of one of the player's games in their games folder with work: newer-build (the sheet's game, or the first of the player's); the Apple ID sign-in, with Apple's request for a verification code with work: code, or after Apple refused it for too many requests, with the wait under way, with work: too-many; a certificate iOS no longer accepts, with work: certificate; the setup after a sign-in that stopped before the certificate, with why it stopped and its report to copy, with work: sign-in-unfinished; the sheet's game, or the first of the player's, paused behind the console, with work: paused; the player's NAS out of reach, away from home, with a newer build of that game in its games folder and two games' saves waiting for it, with work: offline; Add your Mac (screen: storage-mac), the form that pairs this iPhone with a Mac nearby: two Macs whose Cartouche Builder shares with Cartouche, with work: mac-nearby, pairing with the first, with the six digits on both screens, with work: mac-code, or none, iOS refusing Cartouche the local network, with work: mac-refused; the Storage page with the player's Mac, paired, as the games folder and the saves folder, with work: mac, and that Mac out of reach, away from home, with two games' saves waiting for it, with work: mac-offline; the first game's guide after No thanks to its Mac step, with work: build-skipped; what the player says of the sheet's game (screen: gameinfo), and that game, or the first of the player's, with a cover of the player's own, with work: own-cover; Add Google Drive (screen: storage-drive), with the player's own client, and the steps that make it (screen: storage-drive-guide); the player's Google Drive as the games folder and the saves folder, whose sign-in Google ended, as after 7 days for a project in testing, with two games' saves waiting for it, with work: drive-signed-out. The TV (screen: tv) while the sheet's game runs behind the console: its card, where the game leaves its own scene on the TV empty, and paused, with work: paused, at 960 x 540 points, a 1080p TV at 2x. A scenario is drawn as the iPhone of catalog/devices.json shows it (iPhone19,4), or as the model it names (iPad15,3, the 11-inch iPad Air), whose words then call it the iPad. A scenario with a width and a height is drawn at that size in points, with the safe area of that iPhone or iPad, on an iPad: the iPhone 17 Pro, and the iPhone Duo folded (466 x 678) and unfolded (626 x 890), from Apple's pixel sizes at 3x; the iPad mini (744 x 1133) and the 11-inch iPad Air (820 x 1180) upright, and a third of that iPad Air on its side, a window of Cartouche beside two others (375 x 820). A scenario with a device takes the whole screen of that simulator, with its own safe area, size classes and system bars, as on the iPhone Duo and the 13-inch iPad Pro; a landscape one turns the gallery sideways, as a game does, while the simulator stays upright.
